description: Three-dimensional visualization of functions, surfaces, volumes and vector fields, from symbolic formulas or from sampled data. All of these produce Graphics3D objects that can be rotated interactively and combined with Show.

tools.name: Plot3D
tools.description: Plots a surface z = f(x, y) over a rectangular domain, adaptively refining where the function varies quickly. Multiple functions can be drawn in one picture as a list. Use it for any explicit scalar function of two variables.
tools.usage:
Plot3D[f, {x, xmin, xmax}, {y, ymin, ymax}, opts]
Plot3D[{f1, f2}, {x, ...}, {y, ...}]

parameters.name: PlotPoints
parameters.description: Initial sampling grid; raise it for sharp features.

parameters.name: MeshFunctions
parameters.description: Functions whose level curves are drawn as mesh lines.

parameters.name: ColorFunction
parameters.description: Color mapping, by default a function of scaled height.

parameters.name: BoxRatios
parameters.description: Relative lengths of the bounding box edges.

tools.notes: Use RegionFunction to restrict the surface to a subregion, and Exclusions for poles or branch cuts.

tools.name: ListPlot3D
tools.description: Builds a surface from a matrix of heights or from a list of {x, y, z} triples, interpolating scattered points onto a mesh. It is the data counterpart of Plot3D. Use it for gridded measurements, terrain and simulation output.

parameters.name: DataRange
parameters.description: x and y ranges that the array spans.

parameters.name: InterpolationOrder
parameters.description: 0 gives flat facets, 1 linear, 3 smooth.

tools.notes: For irregular point clouds where no single-valued surface exists, use ListSurfacePlot3D instead.

tools.name: ListPointPlot3D
tools.description: Plots a set of three-dimensional points as a scatter cloud without connecting them. Points can be colored and sized by value. Use it for raw 3D data, clustering results and sampled trajectories.

tools.name: ListSurfacePlot3D
tools.description: Reconstructs a surface that passes through an unstructured cloud of 3D points, including closed or multi-valued surfaces. Unlike ListPlot3D it does not require z to be a function of x and y. Use it for scanned objects and isosurface point sets.
tools.notes: For a watertight mesh from a point cloud consider ConvexHullMesh or a Delaunay-based approach.

tools.name: ParametricPlot3D
tools.description: Plots a space curve with one parameter or a parametric surface with two parameters. It handles self-intersecting and closed shapes that cannot be written as z = f(x, y). Use it for knots, tubes, tori and any surface given in parametric form.
tools.usage:
ParametricPlot3D[{fx, fy, fz}, {t, tmin, tmax}]
ParametricPlot3D[{fx, fy, fz}, {u, ...}, {v, ...}, opts]

parameters.name: PlotStyle
parameters.description: Surface directives, or Tube[r] to thicken a curve.

parameters.name: Mesh
parameters.description: Parameter mesh lines on the surface.

tools.example:
ParametricPlot3D[{(2 + Cos[v]) Cos[u], (2 + Cos[v]) Sin[u], Sin[v]},
  {u, 0, 2 Pi}, {v, 0, 2 Pi}, Mesh -> None, PlotStyle -> Opacity[0.8]]

tools.name: ContourPlot3D
tools.description: Draws isosurfaces of a function of three variables, or the surface defined by an equation in x, y and z. Several contour levels can be shown at once with transparency. Use it for implicit surfaces, equipotentials and level sets of 3D fields.

parameters.name: Contours
parameters.description: Number of isosurfaces or explicit level values.

parameters.name: ContourStyle
parameters.description: Styles applied to each isosurface.

tools.example:
ContourPlot3D[x^2 + y^2 - z^2, {x, -2, 2}, {y, -2, 2}, {z, -2, 2},
  Contours -> {-1, 0, 1}, ContourStyle -> Opacity[0.5]]
tools.notes: For sampled 3D arrays use ListContourPlot3D, and for a volumetric view use DensityPlot3D.

tools.name: ListContourPlot3D
tools.description: Extracts isosurfaces from a three-dimensional array of values, interpolating between samples. It is the standard way to view volumetric simulation or imaging data as surfaces. Use Contours to pick the levels of interest.
tools.example:
vol = Table[Exp[-(x^2 + y^2 + z^2)], {x, -2, 2, 0.2}, {y, -2, 2, 0.2}, {z, -2, 2, 0.2}];
ListContourPlot3D[vol, Contours -> {0.2, 0.6}, ContourStyle -> Opacity[0.4]]

tools.name: RegionPlot3D
tools.description: Renders the solid three-dimensional region where a predicate is True. It accepts logical combinations of inequalities and symbolic regions such as Ball or ImplicitRegion. Use it for feasible volumes, intersections of solids and domain visualization.
tools.example:
RegionPlot3D[x^2 + y^2 + z^2 < 1 && z > x y, {x, -1, 1}, {y, -1, 1}, {z, -1, 1},
  PlotPoints -> 50, Mesh -> None]
tools.notes: For measure computations on the same region use RegionMeasure or Volume with ImplicitRegion.

tools.name: SphericalPlot3D
tools.description: Plots a radial function r(theta, phi) in spherical coordinates, producing a closed surface around the origin. It is ideal for spherical harmonics, radiation patterns and angular distributions. Colors can be mapped to the radius to emphasize lobes.
tools.usage: SphericalPlot3D[r, {theta, tmin, tmax}, {phi, pmin, pmax}, opts]
tools.example:
SphericalPlot3D[Abs[SphericalHarmonicY[3, 1, t, p]], {t, 0, Pi}, {p, 0, 2 Pi},
  Mesh -> None, ColorFunction -> "Rainbow"]
tools.notes: The Wolfram convention is r(theta, phi) with theta the polar angle measured from the z axis.

tools.name: RevolutionPlot3D
tools.description: Creates a surface of revolution by rotating a curve about an axis, given either as a height function or parametrically. Partial revolutions are possible by restricting the angular range. Use it for lathe-like shapes, vases, nozzles and volumes of revolution.
tools.usage:
RevolutionPlot3D[fz, {t, tmin, tmax}]
RevolutionPlot3D[{fx, fz}, {t, ...}, {theta, tmin, tmax}, opts]

parameters.name: RevolutionAxis
parameters.description: Axis of revolution, e.g. {0, 0, 1} or {1, 0, 0}.

tools.example:
RevolutionPlot3D[{2 + Cos[t], Sin[t]}, {t, 0, 2 Pi}, {q, 0, 3 Pi/2},
  Mesh -> None]

tools.name: VectorPlot3D
tools.description: Draws arrows sampling a three-dimensional vector field inside a box. Arrow size and color encode magnitude. Use it for electromagnetic fields, velocity fields and gradients in 3D.

parameters.name: VectorPoints
parameters.description: Number of sample points per direction.

parameters.name: VectorColorFunction
parameters.description: Color mapping for arrow magnitude.

tools.name: StreamPlot3D
tools.description: Traces streamlines of a three-dimensional vector field, showing particle paths through the volume. Seed points and line density are controllable. Use it for magnetic field lines, 3D flow and dynamical-system trajectories.

tools.name: ListVectorPlot3D
tools.description: Plots a 3D vector field supplied as a rank-4 array of vector components or as explicit position/vector pairs. It is the data version of VectorPlot3D. Use it for simulation output on a regular grid.

tools.name: ListStreamPlot3D
tools.description: Draws streamlines through a sampled three-dimensional vector field. The field is interpolated before integration, so smoothly varying data works best. Use it with CFD or electromagnetic solver output.

tools.name: DensityPlot3D
tools.description: Renders a scalar function of three variables as a semi-transparent volume, with color and opacity mapped to value. It shows internal structure that isosurfaces alone would hide. Use it for density fields, probability clouds and medical volumes.

parameters.name: ColorFunction
parameters.description: Color gradient applied to scaled values.

parameters.name: OpacityFunction
parameters.description: Maps value to opacity so that low values fade out.

tools.example:
DensityPlot3D[Exp[-(x^2 + y^2 + z^2)], {x, -2, 2}, {y, -2, 2}, {z, -2, 2},
  ColorFunction -> "TemperatureMap", PlotLegends -> Automatic]

tools.name: ListDensityPlot3D
tools.description: Volume-renders a three-dimensional array of values with color and opacity mapped to the data. It is the data counterpart of DensityPlot3D. Use it for CT/MRI stacks and gridded simulation fields.

tools.name: SliceContourPlot3D
tools.description: Draws contour lines of a 3D scalar field on selected slicing surfaces such as planes, boxes or spheres. This gives a cut-away view without full volume rendering. Use it to inspect interior structure along chosen cross-sections.

parameters.name: surf
parameters.description: Slice specification: an equation, "CenterPlanes", "BackPlanes", a region, etc.

tools.name: SliceDensityPlot3D
tools.description: Shades slicing surfaces through a 3D scalar field by value, producing cross-sectional heat maps inside a volume. Slice surfaces can be coordinate planes, a box shell, a sphere or any region. Use it as a lightweight alternative to volume rendering.

tools.name: SliceVectorPlot3D
tools.description: Plots vectors of a 3D field only on chosen slicing surfaces, which keeps the picture readable compared with filling the whole box. Use it to study how a field behaves across a plane or a shell. All VectorPlot3D styling options apply.

tools.name: ListSliceContourPlot3D
tools.description: Draws contours of sampled volumetric data on specified slicing surfaces. It works directly from a 3D array, interpolating onto the slices. Use it when the field comes from measurement or a solver rather than a formula.
tools.example:
vol = Table[Sin[x/3] Cos[y/3] z, {x, 20}, {y, 20}, {z, 20}];
ListSliceContourPlot3D[vol, "CenterPlanes", Contours -> 8]

tools.name: ListSliceDensityPlot3D
tools.description: Shades slices through sampled 3D data by value. It combines the convenience of array input with the readability of cross-sections. Use it for quick inspection of imaging or simulation volumes.

tools.name: ComplexPlot3D
tools.description: Plots the magnitude of a complex function as a surface over the complex plane, coloring it by the argument. Poles rise to infinity and zeros dip to zero while the hue tracks phase. It is the standard 3D view of an analytic function.
tools.example:
ComplexPlot3D[(z - 1)/(z^2 + z + 1), {z, -2 - 2 I, 2 + 2 I},
  PlotLegends -> Automatic]
tools.notes: Use PlotRange to clip the towers around poles; the default already clips sensibly.

tools.name: ListLinePlot3D
tools.description: Plots lists of three-dimensional points as connected lines in space, one polyline per dataset. Use it for 3D trajectories, parametric curves sampled from data and waterfall-style families of curves. Coloring and styling follow the usual plot options.
tools.usage:
ListLinePlot3D[{{x1, y1, z1}, ...}]
ListLinePlot3D[{curve1, curve2, ...}, opts]
tools.example:
curves = Table[Table[{t, k, Sin[t + k]}, {t, 0, 2 Pi, 0.1}], {k, 1, 5}];
ListLinePlot3D[curves, PlotStyle -> Thick]

tools.name: VectorDisplacementPlot3D
tools.description: Shows the deformation of a 3D region under a displacement vector field, drawing the deformed shape and optionally coloring it by a scalar such as stress. It is designed for structural-mechanics results from NDSolve with finite elements. Use it to visualize solid mechanics solutions.
tools.usage:
VectorDisplacementPlot3D[{dx, dy, dz}, reg, opts]
VectorDisplacementPlot3D[{{dx, dy, dz}, s}, reg, opts]

tools.name: Image3D
tools.description: Represents a three-dimensional voxel image built from a stack of 2D slices or a rank-3 array. It renders as an interactive volume and works with many image-processing functions. Use it for microscopy stacks, CT volumes and any voxel data.

parameters.name: ColorFunction
parameters.description: Mapping from voxel value to color.

parameters.name: Boxed
parameters.description: Whether to draw the bounding box.

tools.notes: Image3DSlices extracts 2D slices; many filters such as GaussianFilter work directly on Image3D.

tools.name: ArrayPlot3D
tools.description: Renders a rank-3 array as a solid block of colored voxels, one cube per element. Unlike ListDensityPlot3D it does not interpolate, so discrete structure stays crisp. Use it for cellular automaton states, occupancy grids and label volumes.

tools.name: Graphics3D
tools.description: Assembles 3D graphics primitives and directives into an interactive three-dimensional scene. It is what every 3D plotting function ultimately returns, so results can be combined and post-processed. Use it to build custom scenes or to overlay annotations on plots.

parameters.name: Lighting
parameters.description: Light sources, e.g. "Neutral" or an explicit list.

parameters.name: ViewPoint
parameters.description: Camera position, e.g. {1.3, -2.4, 2} or Front/Top.

parameters.name: Boxed
parameters.description: Whether to draw the bounding box.

tools.example:
Graphics3D[{Opacity[0.6], Red, Sphere[{0, 0, 0}, 1],
  Blue, Cuboid[{1, -0.5, -0.5}, {2, 0.5, 0.5}]}, Lighting -> "Neutral"]
tools.notes: Show combines Graphics3D objects with 3D plots as long as their coordinate systems agree.

tools.name: GraphPlot3D
tools.description: Lays out and draws a graph in three dimensions, which often untangles networks that overlap badly in 2D. It supports the same vertex and edge styling options as GraphPlot. Use it for medium-sized networks and molecular or lattice structures.
